rationale: The configured generic extcon framework must not reuse a connector ID until device_unregister has removed its device name. The release callback in pinned LTS is empty and object storage has separate ownership, so moving ida_free afterward does not dereference freed extcon storage. This prevents registration collisions without changing LTS lifetime rules.

The SDK uses ext4 and enables Unicode/casefold support. Pinned LTS still invalidates a casefolded dentry while holding a journal handle; eviction of child dentries can wait on that transaction, causing a deadlock. Stop the transaction before d_invalidate and guard invalidation on successful removal. The cherry-pick preserves all other newer LTS namei fixes and closes an availability failure.

F2FS remains enabled for Android configuration compatibility. Pinned LTS has the inline-directory conversion bounds check but lacks this lookup check. Reject an on-disk name length above F2FS_NAME_LEN or extending past the available filename slots before comparing it. This prevents out-of-bounds reads from malformed directory entries; existing LTS error cleanup and inode validation are unchanged.
